text: Should you wait until marriage before you lose your virginity? Question that for some reason I receive relatively often. Hey man, first of all, I want to say that I love your content and that you truly guide a whole generation of young men on the right track. I'm curious about your opinion on waiting until marriage before losing your virginity. Do you think as men that is a goal worth following, or do you think we as men should have some experience before actually settling down? My family and friends think that, especially in this generation, waiting till marriage as a man is stupid, but I still don't know if I should listen to them as I am Christian Orthodox. Have a nice day, man, and thank you for your time. To answer your question, we need to agree on the frame. My frame here is this. First, you want to maximize your chances of living a great life as a man when it comes to dating and relationships. Second, if you have sex only after marriage, it means that technically you married your first woman. So from that perspective, think about this. What is the divorce rate in most Western countries? This is a question-answer video, not a research one, so I leave it to you to go check the exact data, but as far as I know, it is somewhere around 40 to 50% in a lot of them. So for simplicity, call it one out of every two marriages ending in divorce. And of the ones that don't divorce, how many are actually happy? A lot of them stay together for the kids, finances, family, or society pressure. So the real number of marriages that actually work is even lower than half. Now here's the part a lot of people miss. A marriage is not a random pairing. It is the relationship that already survived the whole filter. These two people dated, got to know each other, probably lived together, decided they were compatible enough to commit for life. And even after all that filtering, half of them still fail. So if the relationships that passed many tests fail that often, what do you think the odds are for a first relationship that was barely tested at all? And in your case, you are not just betting on your first relationship. You would also be locking it in for life before knowing one of the biggest variables there is, whether the two of you are sexually compatible. Most couples figure that out earlier before they seriously commit. You would be finding out after it's already permanent. So knowing all that, purely from a mathematical perspective, what are the odds that marrying the first woman you've ever been with would lead you to a happy relationship? I would say even 5% could sound too optimistic. Imagine if you wanted to jump with a parachute and the odds of survival would be 5%. Would you do it? So since the odds are stacked like that, what can you actually do to tilt them in your favor? In my opinion, there's only one real option. Get knowledge and experience. And those two work together. Knowledge is having principles and boundaries, self-respect, self-love, knowing what is and is not acceptable in a good relationship, which qualities to look for in a partner, and which qualities to build in yourself. But knowing it is one thing. Applying it is another. That is where experience comes in. You need to meet enough women, go on enough dates, be in enough situations and relationships, sleep with enough women, so you can see from a practical standpoint what actually works for you and what does not. That is what connects the knowledge to reality. Without the experience, the knowledge is just theory. Without the knowledge, the experience is just random. And then when you do choose someone to be with seriously, or to marry, that choice is not a guess. It is built on everything you learn and live through. You know what you are looking for, and you have become the kind of man who can actually match it. So that is why marrying the first woman you are ever with as a virgin is going all in and putting everything on a single number. You are choosing not to learn the game before you bet your whole life on one hand. So no, don't do it. Get the knowledge, get the experience, and then make a choice you can actually stand behind.
